## Genome Binning Using MetaBAT2

Following metagenome assembly with Flye, the assembled contigs were grouped into genome bins using MetaBAT2. The purpose of binning was to separate contigs that potentially originated from the same microbial population, allowing individual metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to be reconstructed from the Black Band Disease (BBD) microbial community.

MetaBAT2 uses sequence composition and coverage information to group contigs. Coverage values were extracted from the Flye assembly information file and saved as `depths_bbd.txt`. The assembly sequences were then reordered to match the coverage file before running MetaBAT2.

### Binning Results

MetaBAT2 produced the following results:

| Binning metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Number of bins | 70 |
| Total sequence length assigned to bins | 39,561,707 bp |
| Total Flye assembly length | 66,634,308 bp |
| Percentage of assembly assigned to bins | 59.4% |

MetaBAT2 generated 70 genome bins containing approximately 39.56 Mb of assembled sequences, representing 59.4% of the total Flye assembly length.

These bins represent preliminary groupings of contigs that may correspond to individual microbial genomes. However, the number of bins does not necessarily represent the number of microbial species present, as some bins may be incomplete or contain sequences from multiple organisms.

The resulting bins were saved as individual FASTA files in `metabat/bins_bbd/` for subsequent assessment of genome completeness and contamination using CheckM.

### Processing Log

The following commands were run in the `metabat/` directory.

First, the coverage information was extracted from the Flye assembly information file:

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/metabat

cat ../flye/bbd/assembly_info.txt | grep -v '#' | awk '{OFS="\t";print $1,$3}' > depths_bbd.txt
```

The `grep -v '#'` command excluded comment lines, while `awk` extracted the contig identifiers and their corresponding coverage values.

Next, the assembled sequences were reordered to match the coverage file:

```{bash}
cat depths_bbd.txt | awk '{print $1}' | xargs samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta > assembly_bbd_ordered.fasta
```

This produced `assembly_bbd_ordered.fasta`, containing the contigs in the same order as the coverage information.

Finally, MetaBAT2 was run to group the contigs into genome bins:

```{bash}
metabat2 -i assembly_bbd_ordered.fasta -a depths_bbd.txt --cvExt -o bins_bbd/metabat --seed 5
```

The `-i` option specified the input assembly, `-a` provided the coverage information, and `-o` specified the output prefix for the genome bins. The `--cvExt` option enabled the use of the supplied coverage information, while `--seed 5` set the random seed for reproducibility.

The resulting genome bins were then used for quality assessment with CheckM.
